newsitem.title: USA: Procter & Gamble off after Q1 report.
newsitem.headline: Procter & Gamble off after Q1 report.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co was off 3-1/4 to 93 Thursday after its first quarter report despite posting earnings of $1.39 a share, two cents above analysts' expectations. First Call's range of estimates was $1.35-$1.38 a share with a mean of $1.37.
Most analysts declined comment, saying they preferred to wait until after P&G's analysts-only conference call scheduled for 1030 EDT/1430 GMT.
But Wesley Roberts of JJB Hilliard, LW Lyons said his initial impression was that the stock was "probably (off) because the top line was pretty weak."

P&G chief executive officer John Pepper warned at the consumer products giant's annual meeting in October that volume and sales results for the quarter would be "below what we have traditionally achieved."
Worldwide unit volume grew one percent from last year's first quarter but sales were down one percent to $8.9 billion from the year-ago $9.03 billion, P&G said in its statement.
